name: Amsterdam
description: Central Amsterdam from the IJ to Museumplein, from open data and the real sun. Every building is the 3DBAG's model of it, measured by the national airborne LiDAR, and every canal house carries the gable of its century.
datum_note: The scene's 0 m is the water level of Amsterdam's canals and the IJ, NAP -0.40 m, which Waternet keeps. AHN removes water from its terrain, so the level is the published one, not a measurement. The viewer's water plane is at 0, so every height in the scene is above the canals; add -0.40 for NAP.

imagery.attribution: Beeldmateriaal Nederland aerial photographs (Actueel ortho HR) via PDOK, CC BY 4.0

terrain.attribution: AHN (Actueel Hoogtebestand Nederland) bare-earth terrain (DTM 0.5 m) via PDOK, CC0; read at 1 m

bag3d.attribution: 3DBAG v2025.09.03 by the 3D geoinformation research group (TU Delft) and 3DGI, from BAG footprints and AHN LiDAR, CC BY 4.0

exclude.why: the Vondelpark's ponds: the park is a polder, its water kept at NAP -2.45 m, two metres below the canals

water.note: The canals, the Amstel and the IJ, all kept at NAP -0.40 m (Ingenieursbureau Amsterdam and Waternet, 2019; Rijkswaterstaat's level decision for the IJ and the Noordzeekanaal). Ponds (class pond) are left to the aerial photo: they lie in parks and polders at levels of their own. Amsterdam is inland (sea false): past the model's edge is land.

trees.note: Species are not mapped; the mix is a guess. Elms line most of the canals, and plane trees the wider streets and squares.

protection.title: No sun rule for public places
protection.summary: Amsterdam has no sun window in law for its squares and parks. Sun on these places is measured for information, not tested against a rule.
protection.source_note: No legal window is transcribed for these places, so each is shown for 10:00-14:00 and none is marked protected.
protection.reading_note: Heights come from the 3DBAG: the national airborne LiDAR (AHN3 to AHN5, 2014-2023) over the cadastral footprints, roof by roof.

reference_heights.source: westerkerk.nl, oudekerk.nl, paleisamsterdam.nl, Ons Amsterdam, amsterdam-monumentenstad.nl, and the Dutch and English Wikipedia (each row's source column)

tour.title: Amsterdam from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings, each the 3DBAG's model of a building in the national register, measured by the national airborne LiDAR. For {share:3dbag}% of the footprint area the height is not a guess.

tour.title: The canal ring
tour.text: {landmark:canal_houses.n} canal houses: brick fronts three windows wide on lots 6 to 8 m wide, under steep roofs whose ridges run back from the canal. {landmark:roofs.gabled_pct}% of the pitched roofs the 3DBAG measured are gabled.

tour.title: A gable for every century
tour.text: Each house ends in the gable of the year it was built: step gables to the 1660s, then neck and bell gables, then the straight cornice. {landmark:canal_houses.gables} fronts carry one: {landmark:canal_houses.by_type.step} step, {landmark:canal_houses.by_type.neck} neck, {landmark:canal_houses.by_type.bell} bell, {landmark:canal_houses.by_type.cornice} cornice and {landmark:canal_houses.by_type.spout} spout.

tour.title: The Westertoren
tour.text: Hendrick de Keyser's tower, finished in 1638: 85 m, the tallest church tower in the city. The laser cannot draw a spire, so the tower is built from its published height.

tour.title: Below the water
tour.text: The canals are kept at 40 cm below NAP, the national datum, and so is the IJ. Most streets in the old city stand a metre or two above the water; the Vondelpark is a polder two metres lower still.

tour.title: Dam, 21 December
tour.text: Midwinter: at noon the sun stands 14 degrees above the horizon in Amsterdam. {sun:Dam|12-21|12:38}% of the square is in direct sun at solar noon.

tour.title: Where the heights come from
tour.text: Coloured by height source: measured by the 3DBAG in the darkest shade. The houseboats in the canals are not in the register, and their heights are a guess.

sources.buildings_3dbag: 3DBAG v2025.09.03 (TU Delft 3D geoinformation group and 3DGI), CC BY 4.0: BAG footprints, AHN heights, LOD1.3 tiers and LOD2.2 roofs
sources.landmarks: Tower heights: westerkerk.nl, oudekerk.nl and the Dutch Wikipedia; canal bridges from their OpenStreetMap outlines
sources.water_level: Canals at NAP -0.40 m: Ingenieursbureau Amsterdam and Waternet, Grondwater effecten van onderkeldering in Amsterdam (2019); the IJ: Rijkswaterstaat's level decision for the Noordzeekanaal and Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal (ANW 92/5850)
sources.gables: Gable dates: Grachtenmuseum, Architecture in the canal district (grachten.museum)

game.title: Amsterdam on Foot
game.blurb: Walk the canal ring and read its gables, take the free ferry across the IJ, and find the winter sun in the old city. Talk to the people who know it. Every fact they tell you comes from the model.
game.ferry_note: Wharves are from OpenStreetMap via Overture. GVB's F3 to Buiksloterweg leaves every 6 minutes by day and crosses in under five, and F2 to IJplein every 15 minutes; both are free for walkers and cyclists (gvb.nl, eyefilm.nl). The game's timetable is not real, and the vessel names are invented.

ferry_style.note: The shared double-ended harbour ferry stands in for GVB's IJ ferries, which are double-ended too; the white and blue are approximate.

vehicles.note: The shared ferry (web/assets/vehicles) in ferry_style's white and blue; no helicopter flies over the old city.

npcs.name: Sanne
idle: Every building here is in the national register, the BAG, and every one was measured by the national laser survey, the AHN. The 3DBAG puts the two together.
There are four trig stations, a triangle on the map for each. Climb up to one and survey the view.

npcs.name: Pieter
idle: A canal house is three windows wide, because the city taxed the width of a front.
Look up. The gable tells you when a house was built, give or take a generation.

npcs.name: Femke
idle: Fifty bells up there. I play them on Tuesdays at noon.
The crown on the tower is the imperial crown of Maximilian. The city has carried it in its arms since 1489.

npcs.name: Joost
idle: The ferries across the IJ are free. Walk on, ride on, no ticket.
Every six minutes by day. You'll never wait long for the F3.

npcs.name: Noor
idle: North of the IJ was shipyards and oil tanks. Now it's the Eye, and the A'DAM tower.
From here the old city is a skyline of church towers. Count them.

npcs.name: Mei
idle: In December the sun is up for seven and a half hours, and it never climbs above fifteen degrees.
In winter we all sit on the side of the square the sun reaches.

npcs.name: Fatima
idle: Stroopwafels, fresh. The syrup has to run.
The market has been on this street since 1905.

lines.title: Report back
lines.on_open: All three surveys done. Report back to Sanne on the Dam.

quests.title: Welcome to the Dam
talk: Hoi! You're the new surveyor? Welcome to the Dam, where Amsterdam began: a dam in the Amstel, around 1270.

The model around you is open data: {buildings} buildings from the 3DBAG, on the national laser-scanned terrain, under the national aerial photographs. For {share:3dbag}% of the footprint area the height was measured, not guessed.
Three surveys today, in any order. The canal ring, with Pieter on the Herengracht. The IJ, with Joost at the ferries behind Centraal Station. And the winter sun, with Mei on the Rembrandtplein.

choices.text: The canal ring: Pieter, on the Herengracht
The IJ: Joost, at the ferries behind Centraal Station
The winter sun: Mei, on the Rembrandtplein

quests.title: Read a gable
talk: Ah, the surveyor. Sanne said you'd come. The canal ring was dug from 1613, and most of these houses were built in the hundred years after.

Each front ends in the gable of its day. Step gables until the 1660s, then the neck gable, then the bell, and from the 1700s the straight cornice. This model draws each house's gable from the year the register gives for it.
Aim at a house and press Q for the survey lens. Find me a step gable, a neck gable and a bell gable. Then go up to the Westertoren; Femke plays its bells.

steps.text: Survey lens (Q): find a step gable, a neck gable and a bell gable
Find Femke at the foot of the Westertoren

quests.title: The Westertoren
talk: Hello. You found the tallest church tower in the city: 85 metres, 87 with the weathercock. Hendrick de Keyser designed it, and it was finished in 1638.
A laser over a ten-metre footprint can't draw a spire, so the model builds it from its published height, with Maximilian's crown on top.

Two doors down the Prinsengracht is number 263, the Anne Frank House. Anne could hear these bells from the Secret Annex, every quarter of an hour. Walk past it, then tell Sanne the canal ring is surveyed.

steps.text: Walk to the Anne Frank House, Prinsengracht 263

quests.title: Across the IJ
talk: Morning! Off to the north bank? The F3 goes to Buiksloterweg, the Eye is right there.
It's free, it runs day and night, and it takes less than five minutes. The IJ is kept at the same level as the canals, 40 centimetres below NAP.
When you're over, find Noor at the Eye. She knows the north bank.

steps.text: Ride the F3 from Centraal Station to Buiksloterweg
Find Noor at the Eye Filmmuseum

quests.title: The north bank
talk: Welcome to Noord. That tower is the A'DAM Toren, Shell's offices from 1971. Now there's a swing on the roof.
The laser's highest point on it is {landmark:adam_toren.height_m} m above the street. Published, it's 80 m to the roof and about 100 m to the top of the mast: the laser caught the mast.
Walk to its foot and look up. Then you can tell Sanne the IJ is surveyed.

steps.text: Walk to the foot of the A'DAM Toren

quests.title: Sun in December
talk: Hi! You're the surveyor? Perfect. I'm writing about the sun in the city in winter.
On the 21st of December the sun stands 14 degrees above the horizon at noon, which is at 12:38 here. The houses round this square are 15 to 20 metres tall, so their shadows are 60 to 80 metres long.
Find me a spot on the Rembrandtplein in direct sun between 10 and 2 on the 21st. Then go to the Albert Cuyp market and buy a stroopwafel from Fatima. I'll pay you back.

steps.text: Stand in direct sun on the Rembrandtplein, 10:00 to 14:00 on 21 December
Find Fatima at the Albert Cuyp market

quests.title: A stroopwafel
talk: Goedemiddag! A stroopwafel? Wait, I'll make it fresh. Two thin waffles, syrup in between, warm so it runs.
Mei sent you? Then it's on her. Tell her the sun is surveyed, and tell Sanne too.

quests.title: Survey complete
talk: You're back. The canal ring, the IJ and the winter sun: that's Amsterdam, read from the register and the laser.
Every house you looked at was measured, and every shadow comes from the sun's real position. If something looks wrong, it is probably wrong in the data. Tell the 3DBAG, or fix OpenStreetMap.
Doei, surveyor. The city is yours to walk.
